claims.title: Hatshepsut's expedition to Punt
claims.summary: Reliefs at Queen Hatshepsut's temple at Deir el-Bahri record a major Egyptian trading voyage to the Land of Punt, returning with myrrh trees, incense, gold and ivory—the most celebrated ancient evidence of the trade.

sources.label: Middle Portico South (Portico of Punt)
sources.publisher: Polish-Egyptian Archaeological and Conservation Expedition, University of Warsaw

claims.title: Egyptian trade with Punt begins
claims.summary: Egyptian records attest trading contact with Punt from the Old Kingdom onward, drawing the Horn of Africa into pharaonic commerce in aromatic resins and luxury goods.

sources.label: Middle Portico South (Portico of Punt)
sources.publisher: Polish-Egyptian Archaeological and Conservation Expedition, University of Warsaw

claims.title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
claims.summary: A Greek mariner's handbook describes ports along the Horn coast trading frankincense, myrrh, ivory and tortoiseshell with Egypt, Arabia and India, documenting the region's role in Indian Ocean commerce.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-60-periplus-of-the-erythraean-sea, claim TL:SOM:event:60:periplus-of-the-erythraean-sea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cushitic pastoralists spread across the Horn
claims.summary: Cushitic-speaking herding peoples, ancestral to the Somalis, expand across the arid interior of the Horn of Africa, establishing the pastoral, clan-based society that would endure into modern times.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-100-cushitic-pastoralists-spread-across-the-horn, claim TL:SOM:event:100:cushitic-pastoralists-spread-across-the-horn, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islam established on the Somali coast
claims.summary: Trade and migration across the Gulf of Aden carry Islam to the Horn, and Muslim merchant communities take root in the coastal towns that become Somalia's medieval city-states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-900-islam-established-on-the-somali-coast, claim TL:SOM:event:900:islam-established-on-the-somali-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zeila, Berbera and Mogadishu flourish
claims.summary: The ports of Zeila, Berbera and Mogadishu grow wealthy on Indian Ocean trade with Arabia, Persia and India; Mogadishu mints its own coinage and becomes a leading commercial centre.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1000-zeila-berbera-and-mogadishu-flourish, claim TL:SOM:event:1000:zeila-berbera-and-mogadishu-flourish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ibn Battuta visits Mogadishu
claims.summary: The traveller Ibn Battuta describes Mogadishu as a large, prosperous Muslim trading city, attesting to the wealth of the Benadir coast in the medieval Indian Ocean world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1331-ibn-battuta-visits-mogadishu, claim TL:SOM:event:1331:ibn-battuta-visits-mogadishu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wars of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi
claims.summary: From the Adal Sultanate, Imam Ahmad 'Gurey' launches the Futuh al-Habasha campaigns against Christian Ethiopia, conquering much of the highlands before his defeat and death in 1543 with Portuguese intervention.

sources.label: Somalia: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Death of Ahmad and decline of Adal
claims.summary: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi is killed in battle against an Ethiopian–Portuguese force, halting the Muslim conquest of the highlands and beginning the decline of the Adal Sultanate.

sources.label: Somalia: A Country Study
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Ajuran Sultanate
claims.summary: The Ajuran empire dominates southern Somalia and the Horn, controlling the Shabelle and Jubba river systems, building wells and fortifications and resisting Oromo and Portuguese incursions before fragmenting in the late 17th century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1300-the-ajuran-sultanate, claim TL:SOM:event:1300:the-ajuran-sultanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Geledi Sultanate
claims.summary: The Sultanate of the Geledi emerges from the breakup of the Ajuran state, with its capital at Afgooye, and under the Gobroon dynasty comes to dominate the trade of southern Somalia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1700-rise-of-the-geledi-sultanate, claim TL:SOM:event:1700:rise-of-the-geledi-sultanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Majeerteen and Hobyo sultanates
claims.summary: In north-eastern Somalia the Majeerteen Sultanate (Migiurtinia) and the Sultanate of Hobyo control the coast and its maritime trade, maintaining centralised authority and treaty relations with outside powers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1800-majeerteen-and-hobyo-sultanates, claim TL:SOM:event:1800:majeerteen-and-hobyo-sultanates, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Geledi at the height of its power
claims.summary: Under Sultan Yusuf Mahamud Ibrahim the Geledi Sultanate reaches its peak, commanding tribute across southern Somalia, before the sultan's death in battle in 1848 begins a gradual decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1843-geledi-at-the-height-of-its-power, claim TL:SOM:event:1843:geledi-at-the-height-of-its-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British Somaliland protectorate
claims.summary: Britain signs treaties with northern Somali clans and establishes a protectorate over the northern coast to safeguard supplies for Aden, creating British Somaliland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1884-british-somaliland-protectorate, claim TL:SOM:event:1884:british-somaliland-protectorate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Italy's protectorates and Italian Somaliland
claims.summary: Italy signs protectorate treaties with the Hobyo and Majeerteen sultanates and occupies the Benadir coast, building up Italian Somaliland in the south; the Benadir colony is formally established in 1905.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1889-italy-s-protectorates-and-italian-somaliland, claim TL:SOM:event:1889:italy-s-protectorates-and-italian-somaliland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Dervish resistance
claims.summary: Sayyid Mohammed Abdullah Hassan leads the Dervish movement in a twenty-year armed struggle against British, Italian and Ethiopian forces, defeating several colonial expeditions from fortified bases in the interior.

sources.label: The Somali leader who led a 20-year resistance against colonial powers

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1899-the-dervish-resistance, claim TL:SOM:event:1899:the-dervish-resistance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: RAF bombing ends the Dervish state
claims.summary: Britain uses the Royal Air Force to bomb the Dervish forts, including Taleh; the movement collapses and Sayyid Mohammed Abdullah Hassan dies of illness later that year.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1920-raf-bombing-ends-the-dervish-state, claim TL:SOM:event:1920:raf-bombing-ends-the-dervish-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Italian Somaliland joins Italian East Africa
claims.summary: After Fascist Italy's conquest of Ethiopia, Italian Somaliland is merged into the new colony of Italian East Africa; Britain takes control of the region during the Second World War, holding both Somalilands by 1941.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1936-italian-somaliland-joins-italian-east-africa, claim TL:SOM:event:1936:italian-somaliland-joins-italian-east-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of the Somali Republic
claims.summary: British Somaliland (independent 26 June) and the former Italian Somaliland unite on 1 July 1960 to form the independent Somali Republic, with Aden Abdullah Osman Daar as first president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1960-birth-of-the-somali-republic, claim TL:SOM:event:1960:birth-of-the-somali-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Siad Barre seizes power
claims.summary: Following the assassination of President Shermarke, the army stages a coup and General Mohamed Siad Barre takes control, suspending the constitution and establishing a one-party socialist dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1969-siad-barre-seizes-power, claim TL:SOM:event:1969:siad-barre-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Somali written in Latin script
claims.summary: Barre's government adopts a Latin-based orthography for the Somali language and launches mass literacy campaigns, a lasting cultural achievement of the early socialist period.

sources.label: Socialist Somalia: the legacy of Barre's military regime

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1972-somali-written-in-latin-script, claim TL:SOM:event:1972:somali-written-in-latin-script, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ogaden War
claims.summary: Somalia invades Ethiopia to annex the Somali-inhabited Ogaden; initial gains are reversed in 1978 when the Soviet Union and Cuba back Ethiopia, inflicting a costly defeat on Somalia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1977-the-ogaden-war, claim TL:SOM:event:1977:the-ogaden-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War in the north
claims.summary: Government forces wage a brutal counter-insurgency against the Somali National Movement in the north, bombarding Hargeisa and killing many thousands of civilians as armed opposition spreads.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1988-war-in-the-north, claim TL:SOM:event:1988:war-in-the-north, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Siad Barre
claims.summary: Rebel forces drive Siad Barre from Mogadishu, ending his 21-year dictatorship; with no agreement on a successor, central authority collapses and the country descends into civil war.

sources.label: Somalia (CRS In Focus)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress / Congressional Research Service

claims.title: State collapse and Somaliland's declaration
claims.summary: Central government disappears as faction leaders fight for control; the former British Somaliland declares independence as the Republic of Somaliland, which remains internationally unrecognised but largely self-governing.

sources.label: Somalia (CRS In Focus)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress / Congressional Research Service

claims.title: Famine and Operation Restore Hope
claims.summary: Drought and civil war cause a famine that kills several hundred thousand people; the UN sets up UNOSOM and a US-led force launches Operation Restore Hope in December to safeguard relief.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Somalia: From the incense ports of Punt and the medieval Adal Sultanate to independence in 1960, state collapse and the slow rebuilding of a federal republic.", terralore.co/country/SOM/chronicle#ev-1992-famine-and-operation-restore-hope, claim TL:SOM:event:1992:famine-and-operation-restore-hope, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Mogadishu ('Black Hawk Down')
claims.summary: A US raid against a faction leader turns into a fierce urban battle that kills 18 American and many Somali fighters and civilians, hastening the withdrawal of foreign forces by 1995.

sources.label: Somalia (CRS In Focus)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress / Congressional Research Service

claims.title: Islamic Courts Union and the rise of Al-Shabaab
claims.summary: The Islamic Courts Union briefly controls much of the south before an Ethiopian intervention ousts it; from its militant wing emerges Al-Shabaab, which launches a prolonged jihadist insurgency.

sources.label: Al Shabaab (CRS In Focus)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress / Congressional Research Service

claims.title: Federal Government of Somalia established
claims.summary: A new permanent Federal Government is formed under a provisional constitution—the first central government since 1991—as African Union forces push Al-Shabaab back from major cities.

sources.label: Somalia (CRS In Focus)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress / Congressional Research Service

claims.title: Drought, famine risk and renewed offensive
claims.summary: A severe multi-season drought pushes parts of Somalia toward famine while the Federal Government, backed by local clan militias and international forces, mounts a renewed offensive against Al-Shabaab.
